item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia's CEO, CFO Colette Kress takes over on an interim basis, and the shares open down more than 13%
item.description: Nvidia's co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director with immediate effect; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a successor, and Huang has agreed to testify to Congress. (TechCrunch, BBC, TechCrunch)

item.title: The Fed scraps its October 2027 rate vote and holds no December meeting, so no rate decision is due between mid-November 2027 and late January 2028
item.description: The Fed's revised 2027 calendar keeps eight meetings but turns October's into a strategy session with no rate decision and drops December, part of Chair Kevin Warsh's plan to meet less often. (Federal Reserve, The New York Times)

item.title: US existing-home sales fall 5.5% in October to 3.75 million, the lowest pace since August 2010, as mortgage rates climb
item.description: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5% in October to an annual pace of 3.75 million, down 8.8% from a year earlier, as 30-year mortgage rates hover near 7.18%. (National Association of Realtors, The Guardian)

item.title: Cisco raises its annual revenue forecast to as much as $75.8 billion after a record quarter driven by AI networking
item.description: Cisco's quarterly revenue rose 24% to a record $18.5 billion, beating estimates, and it lifted its fiscal 2027 outlook and its forecast for AI infrastructure sales to cloud giants to $9 billion. (Cisco, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Clearing the Fog: Price Transparency, Market Churn, and Consumer Welfare in Short-Term Rentals
item.description: After California required Airbnb and similar hosts to show fee-inclusive prices, guests became more price-sensitive, nightly rates rose 4.8%, and many fee-heavy listings left the market, with net gains for consumers on average. (Ginger Zhe Jin, Liad Wagman, Jingyi Xing)

item.title: Nvidia's board prepares to replace CEO Jensen Huang, and the stock falls about 8% after hours
item.description: Nvidia's board met to prepare for removing co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after two reported affairs, one with a suspected Chinese spy; the shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading. (TechCrunch, Fortune, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: UK economy grows 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in more than two years
item.description: UK GDP rose 0.7% from July to September, led by services such as computer programming tied to cloud and AI spending, despite higher energy prices from the Iran war. (Office for National Statistics, BBC)

item.title: EU court adviser says Google's annulled 1.49 billion euro AdSense fine was wrongly scrapped
item.description: Advocate General Juliane Kokott told the EU's top court that a lower court erred in 2024 when it annulled Google's AdSense fine, and proposed sending the case back for a new ruling. (TNW, EU Law Live)

item.title: Canadian Tire beats profit estimates as higher gas prices lift sales, and raises its dividend
item.description: Canadian Tire's third-quarter profit rose to $246.4 million, beating forecasts, as pricier gasoline boosted sales; comparable sales rose 4.4%, or 1.7% without its gas business. (The Globe and Mail, Canadian Tire Corporation (newswire))

item.title: The Main Monetary Policy Shock
item.description: Combining three kinds of Fed announcement surprises, the authors find monetary policy shocks explain about 18% of swings in consumer prices over four years, far more than prior work suggested. (Christoph Boehm, Husang Kim, T. Niklas Kroner · University of Texas at Austin, Federal Reserve Board of Governors)

item.title: US consumer prices rise 0.4% in October, more than forecast, keeping a December Fed hike in play
item.description: The US consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% analysts expected but slower than September's 0.6%, as energy price increases eased. (The Guardian, BBC News)

item.title: Bank of Canada notes show it hiked because energy costs were starting to spread, and it may go further
item.description: The Bank of Canada's summary of its October 28 deliberations shows officials raised the rate to 2.5% to stop high energy prices becoming broad inflation and did not rule out more hikes. (Bank of Canada)

item.title: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce as it slows its production ramp-up
item.description: Boeing will cut roughly 5% of its commercial airplane staff through layoffs and attrition after slowing plans to raise jet output, with layoff notices starting in December. (The Guardian, KIRO 7 News)

item.title: Children's Place files for bankruptcy and puts its kidswear brands up for sale
item.description: Children's Place, owner of the Gymboree brand, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and set a December 9 deadline for bids on its assets after falling sales and mounting losses. (The Globe and Mail, FashionUnited)

item.title: Unconventional Monetary Policy and Deposit Retention
item.description: Years of zero interest rates and Fed bond buying filled US banks with rate-sensitive depositors, which made keeping deposits costlier and riskier once rates rose in 2015 and 2022. (Philip Strahan, Tuo Yang · Boston College)

item.title: Anthropic sets a $70 to $78 price range for an IPO that could raise up to $64.4 billion
item.description: Anthropic's filing shows an indicative range of $70 to $78 a share and up to $64.4 billion raised, the first public-market test of frontier AI valuations. (The Globe and Mail, TechCrunch)

item.title: Fed's Waller backs a December hike even if October inflation cools, and floats a half-point move
item.description: Governor Waller said he would support a quarter-point hike in December regardless of October's CPI, and a half-point if core prices rose 0.3 percent or more. (Federal Reserve, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: California voters reject a one-time 5% tax on billionaires after a record-spending campaign
item.description: Californians defeated Proposition 40, a one-time 5% wealth tax on residents worth over $1 billion, after opponents spent nearly $425 million. (The Guardian, BBC, TechCrunch)

item.title: Financial Advisors and Retirees' Risk-taking
item.description: Retirees with financial advisors hold about two-thirds of their portfolios in stocks, 30 to 40 percentage points more than comparable retirees without one. (Allison T. Cole, Maarten Meeuwis, Alessandro Previtero et al.)

item.title: Canada launches its instant payments system, the last G7 country to do so
item.description: Payments Canada began the first phase of its Real-Time Rail on Monday, nearly seven years after the original 2019 target, with eight institutions but none of the big banks. (The Globe and Mail, BetaKit)

item.title: Strathcona agrees to buy Greenfire in a deal worth up to C$2.9 billion
item.description: Strathcona Resources will acquire Greenfire Resources for shares or C$11.00 in cash per share, valuing the deal at about C$2.7 to 2.9 billion including debt, with the same fund controlling both. (Greenfire Resources (company release), The Globe and Mail)

item.title: AI as Shared Business Infrastructure: Firm Growth and the Distribution of Gains
item.description: On a Chinese e-commerce platform, small firms that adopted built-in generative AI saw monthly sales rise 51.6%, with the biggest proportional gains for the smallest firms. (Panle Jia Barwick, Lu Fang, Jinhan Liu et al.)

item.title: US hiring surprises at 165,000 jobs while Canada's labour market weakens, with unemployment at 4.1% and 6.7%
item.description: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October versus about 65,000 expected, while Canada lost 4,700 jobs and its unemployment rate rose to 6.7%, widening the gap between the two labour markets. (Statistics Canada, Associated Press via The Globe and Mail, Reuters via The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Canada's 2026 budget moves bank anti-money-laundering supervision to OSFI and proposes tax simplifications
item.description: Ottawa's budget shifts supervision of banks' anti-money-laundering work from FinTRAC to OSFI, offers modest corporate tax simplification, and a follow-on reform loosens temporary foreign worker limits. (Budget 2026, Government of Canada, The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: The Effects of Monetary Policy on Macroeconomic Expectations: High-Frequency Evidence from Prediction Markets
item.description: Using minute-by-minute prices of Kalshi prediction-market contracts, the authors find macro expectations respond to Fed announcements as standard theory predicts, with little or no "Fed information effect". (Eric T. Swanson, Wang Renxuan, Yanbin Wu)

item.title: Wall Street's AI-driven rout deepens after the midterms and spreads across Asia
item.description: US stocks fell sharply on Thursday as investors feared Democratic control of Congress could slow the AI buildout, and the losses spread to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Friday. (The Guardian (live, Nov 6), The Guardian (Nov 4), The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Tesla says it will stop making the Cybertruck next year to make room for the Cybercab
item.description: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in 2027, using the factory space for its two-seat Cybercab robotaxi after years of weak sales. (BBC News, TechCrunch)

item.title: Aggregate-Surplus Maximizing Monetary Policy
item.description: A new NBER paper finds that when households differ in labor-market frictions, a central bank maximizing everyone's joint surplus should weight output stabilization about 37 percent more than inflation, compared with the standard model. (David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein, Joao Guerreiro)

item.title: Bank of England raises its rate to 4%, the first increase in more than three years
item.description: The Bank of England voted 8-1 to lift Bank Rate to 4% from 3.75%, saying energy-driven inflation pressure in the pipeline is now strong enough to justify tighter policy. (Bank of England, BBC, BBC)

item.title: ECB wage tracker points to slightly firmer negotiated pay growth into 2027
item.description: The ECB's wage tracker shows negotiated wage growth of 2.7% in late 2026 and 2.8% in early 2027, a little higher than the 2.3% headline figure for 2026 as a whole. (European Central Bank)

item.title: US trade deficit narrows slightly to $105.0 billion in September as exports and imports both rise
item.description: The US goods and services trade deficit eased by $0.7 billion to $105.0 billion in September, though the three-month average deficit widened to $101.2 billion. (U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis)

item.title: Canada's trade surplus widens to a four-year high as gold and energy offset tariff-hit exports
item.description: Canada's September merchandise trade surplus widened to about C$5.4 billion, the highest since May 2022, but gold and oil hid a 5.6% drop in other exports hit by US tariffs. (Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Demand-Driven Inflation
item.description: Giannone and Primiceri argue that unexpectedly strong demand, not supply shocks alone, drove the post-pandemic inflation surge in both the United States and the euro area. (Domenico Giannone, Giorgio Primiceri · Johns Hopkins University; Northwestern University)

item.title: US tech stocks rebound as an AI-spending selloff ends on election day
item.description: US tech shares recovered on Tuesday after a week-long AI selloff, with oil easing from $117 to $103 a barrel, while investors largely looked past the midterm elections. (The Guardian)

item.title: Canva to cut or relocate 1,271 jobs as growth slows
item.description: Design-software firm Canva is restructuring 22% of its workforce, 1,271 people, after growth slowed for the first time in a decade and AI costs rose. (BBC News, TechCrunch)

item.title: Foodtastic bids $1 billion for MTY Food Group as MTY replaces its CEO
item.description: Foodtastic took a $43-a-share cash offer for MTY directly to shareholders after MTY's board refused talks, on the same day MTY abruptly replaced its CEO. (The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Shopify shares drop 12.8% at the open despite 31.5% revenue growth
item.description: Shopify's third-quarter revenue of US$3.742 billion grew 31.5% but missed analyst expectations by a hair, and the stock fell as expectations were high. (The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US factory orders jump 1.8% in September on aircraft and AI build-out
item.description: New orders for US factory goods rose 1.8% in September, beating the 1.2% forecast, helped by aircraft bookings and AI infrastructure, though economists warn of headwinds next year. (The Globe and Mail (Reuters))
